units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tour done, a few beers in. And it's evening.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How are we doing for dinner?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Dinner is at 6:30 PM, at Cafe de Klos, and it's walk-ins only.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So no booking.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: No booking. You turn up and wait.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a small place and it fills up fast, so we'd suggest going straight there from the brewery.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How far?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: About a kilometer, fifteen minutes on foot.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Walk north, away from the canal, into the old town.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Keep a map open. You're aiming for Kerkstraat, a long street between the canals, near the Vijzelgracht.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the cafe?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Kerkstraat 41. It's a small, dark, cozy bar with a lot of character.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what do we eat?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's known in Amsterdam for spare ribs.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Big plates of them, grilled, with sauces, and garlic.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Local guides often mention the garlic.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Garlic. Spooky, if you think about vampires.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ha. Nicely done. Garlic against vampires is folklore, and of course there are no vampires here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But if you ate a lot of garlic tonight, they'd leave you alone.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the spooky request is covered.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Technically.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: You said walk-ins only. What if there's a queue?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then wait, or have a drink nearby.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There are plenty of bars on the nearby streets.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We can't promise a table, and we can't promise opening hours, so please check before you leave the brewery.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A phone call or a look at a map will do.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Do we have to eat ribs?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: No. They have other dishes. But you don't get this reputation for nothing.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What do you drink with ribs?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You've just come from a brewery.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right. Beer. Or if I'm brave, champagne.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With ribs.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I like to live dangerously.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It would be unusual. But it's your holiday.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Now, Ben, a bet.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Go on.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll lose a napkin before the end of the meal.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You'll lose three, and a sleeve.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Probably true.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause now. Eat. We'll come back at the end.
